[RFCS.23.3] **`schema_hash` fingerprints what decoding depends on.** It is the
SHA-256 of the schema's `SchemaShape` (`proto/fact_external.proto#SchemaShape`):
the schema's own name ([LIMP.13.1]) and, for each slot in byte order of slot name, the slot's
name, its `Kind`, whether it is nullable, for a fact-reference slot the
referenced schema's own name, and for a slot declared `Time`, `Date` or `Duration`
its declared `SlotKind` (`proto/slot.proto#SlotKind`, [RDSC.5.5.8]). So a
`Time` slot and an `Int` slot of the same name hash differently, though both
carry `KIND_INT` ([RFCS.23.2]). The shape is encoded with its fields in field-number
order and default values omitted, so every writer produces the same bytes.

Lifecycle, identity keys, slot order and units are outside the hash: the
receiving program applies its own ([RFCS.23.6]).

A `FactExternal`'s `schema` is the schema's own name. A program must refuse a
`FactExternal` whose `schema_hash` differs from that of its own schema of the
same name, and must refuse one naming a schema it does not declare
([LIMP.13.3]). A record written under a changed schema is read only after migration
([RFCS.23.8]).
